teacher: Matsunami Goro (Hero name: 'Scaffold' — Quirk: Construct, builds rigid scaffolding structures from ambient minerals. Methodical, patient, and quietly competitive about his class.)
reputation: The class that almost made it to 1-A. Their entrance exam scores were comparable — in some technical categories, better. Matsunami runs a tighter ship than Oshiro. 1-B students know their fundamentals cold before they start improvising. Less chaos, more precision. They watch 1-A the way you watch someone doing something impressive badly.
sports_festival_note: Tier 2, Arc 1. Class 1-B enter the Sports Festival as the school's open secret — everyone's picked a 1-A favourite, nobody's thought hard about 1-B. That's exactly how Matsunami wants it. He has drilled his students on 1-A's quirks from the entrance exam footage. This is the arc where 1-B stops being background noise.
dm_overview: Introduce 1-B students gradually through Tier 1 — brief corridor encounters, overheard conversations, cafeteria sightings. None of them are villains. None of them are friends yet. They're rivals in the classical sense: people who make your students better by existing. By the time the Sports Festival starts, players should have a clear read on at least 3-4 of these students and be genuinely unsure who's going to win.

tier1_introduction_guide.arc1_entrance_exam: The results board after the exam shows Class 1-A and 1-B scores in adjacent columns. 1-B's top score (Yamaru Todao: 84 pts) is visible. Whether it beats or matches 1-A's best depends on the session. Fujisaki mentions '1-B had a different site this year — quieter, but thorough.' Oshiro says nothing about 1-B. He doesn't need to.
tier1_introduction_guide.arc2_dorm_life: Yamaru and Domoto are visible in the cafeteria. Yamaru eats without hurry, like nothing that's happened yet has cost him anything. He looks at the 1-A table once, says nothing. Domoto catches the eye of whoever's watching and winks, then covers three seats in a single explosive hop instead of walking. The practice room booking shows 1-B has 6am slots every weekday. Kagamo's warmup rattles the building at 7am. The class notices.
tier1_introduction_guide.arc3_capture_the_flag: Kagamo Akake is watching through the observation window. When a student looks over, she gives an exaggerated double thumbs-up. It's impossible to tell if it's sincere or condescending. Oshiro drops the line: 'Class 1-B had three students who topped this score in their equivalent drill. That's your benchmark.'
tier1_introduction_guide.arc4_agency_visit: Hashige Tataka is at the same agency district for a different internship. If the class encounters him: he's carrying precisely organised equipment cases, gives the impression he's been there three days, and has a 10-second corridor interaction before continuing. He doesn't introduce himself. His name badge faces inward. If a student catches a glimpse: Hashige, T., Class 1-B.

students.name: Kakita Keiko

quirk_mechanics.weakness: A lock must be established with a full action of concentrated study on a visible target, and losing line of sight to that target for a full round breaks it entirely — nothing she throws before establishing a lock behaves any differently than an ordinary thrown weapon.

abilities.name: Lock On
abilities.description: Studies a creature within 60 feet she can see, marking it as locked for up to one minute or until she loses line of sight for a full round. She can maintain one lock at a time (two at 7th level, the second at disadvantage).

abilities.name: Homing Throw
abilities.description: Makes a ranged attack with a thrown weapon against a locked target. The weapon curves around minor obstacles and cover smaller than a solid wall to strike, granting advantage on the attack roll.

students.quirk_summary: Once Kakita has studied a target long enough to lock on, anything she throws afterward curves through the air to find them — around corners, past cover, through a crowd. She can't do it on reflex; the lock takes real concentration to establish. But once it's up, missing isn't really a possibility anymore, which is exactly the kind of certainty she prefers to work with.
students.personality: Calm, precise, and quietly proud of how rarely she misses once she's actually locked on. Talks in short, exact sentences, the same way she throws. Keeps to herself in the back of the room, doodling trajectory lines in the margins of her notes. Flicks her wrist and clicks her tongue before any real throw — a tell her rival in 1-A has started to notice. Never rushes a throw; would rather spend three extra seconds on a clean lock than throw wild and hope.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Scales vs Homing. Ando's natural plating is exactly the kind of surface a thrown weapon struggles to punch through cleanly — a locked throw still has to find the gap between scales, not just find him. Kakita has already worked out where his weak points probably are from exam footage. She hasn't had to use that information yet.
students.sports_festival_role: A backline precision striker in any event with cover or crowding — once she locks a target, thrown objects find them regardless of what's in between. In the tournament bracket, opponents who never let her get a clean three-second study window are the only ones who reliably give her trouble.
students.tier1_appearance: Seen in the practice yard throwing at a target rotated slowly by a training drone, over and over, adjusting nothing visible between throws. A 1-A student watching for a full minute never sees her miss once the lock is up.
students.dm_notes: Kakita is a patience-reward archetype — dull to fight until the lock lands, then suddenly inevitable. Let the lock-establishing beat matter: describe her studying a target, make players feel the window closing. Her rivalry with Ando is a straightforward 'find the gap in the armor' problem she hasn't fully solved yet.
signature_moves: Lock On (Action): studies a visible target within 60ft, marking it locked for up to one minute.
Homing Throw (Action): ranged thrown attack against a locked target with advantage, curving around minor cover.
Double Lock (Passive, 7th level): can maintain a second lock simultaneously, at disadvantage on attacks against the second target.

students.name: Domoto Fumiju

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Her explosive bursts require a running start or a solid surface to push off of — restrained, grappled, or on unstable/loose ground, she moves like anyone else her size.

abilities.name: Kick Off
abilities.description: Explosively pushes off the ground, gaining an additional 20 feet of movement this turn and advantage on the next Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check made as part of the move.

abilities.name: Piston Kick
abilities.description: A leaping kick using stored momentum: 1d10 + Strength modifier bludgeoning damage, and if she used Kick Off this turn, the target must succeed on a Strength save or be knocked prone.

students.quirk_summary: Domoto's legs carry far more force than her frame suggests — a single push sends her covering ground in short, explosive bursts rather than a smooth sprint. Her hearing sharpens the same way, ears standing up and swiveling toward sound whenever she's alert. She uses both constantly and casually, which makes her genuinely disorienting to track in a fight.
students.personality: Bright, twitchy, can't sit still for a full class period — talks fast, moves faster, apologizes for neither. Perpetually mid-fidget: tapping a foot, bouncing a knee, first one out the door when the bell rings. Thumps a foot against the floor twice before every real fight, an old habit she calls luck and everyone else calls nerves. Covers ground in short bursts rather than a straight sprint, which makes her hard to predict because she doesn't plan the route, she just goes.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Overclock vs Rabbit. Ren is faster in a straight line than anyone in either class. Domoto isn't trying to out-run him — she's trying to never be where his straight line ends up, covering ground in bursts he can't extrapolate from a smooth approach vector. Whether unpredictable beats fast is the whole question.
students.sports_festival_role: The worst kind of opponent in any pursuit or containment event — impossible to read a chase against. In the tournament bracket, once she's restrained or knocked off her feet, the explosive advantage disappears completely, which is the only reliable way anyone's beaten her yet.
students.tier1_appearance: First spotted covering the length of the dorm hallway in two bounds to grab the last of the good breakfast, ears flat with concentration the whole way.
students.dm_notes: Domoto should feel fast in bursts, not fast constantly — describe the explosive push, then the recovery beat after. Her hearing is a genuine mechanical asset (advantage on Perception checks by sound) worth using in scenes beyond combat.
signature_moves: Kick Off (Bonus Action): explosive push granting 20 extra feet of movement and advantage on an Athletics/Acrobatics check this turn.
Piston Kick (Action): leaping kick, 1d10 + STR bludgeoning; knocks prone (STR save) if Kick Off was used this turn.
Long Ears (Passive): advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing.

students.name: Hama Kokao

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Locating something requires several seconds of stillness and concentration — forced to keep moving or under active attack, his searching ability is effectively unavailable, and he can only search for something he's directly encountered before (met, held, touched).

abilities.name: Locate
abilities.description: Senses the general direction and rough distance (within 100 feet, closer/farther beyond that) of a specific person or object he's previously met or held, regardless of walls or line of sight.

abilities.name: Read the Room
abilities.description: Spends a moment scanning a space he's already in, gaining advantage on his next Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check made in that location.

students.quirk_summary: A second, smaller pair of eyelids beneath his normal ones opens onto flat, reflective silver irises when he concentrates — and once they're open, Hama can sense the rough direction and distance of anyone or anything he's already encountered, through walls, across floors, regardless of what's in the way. It only works on things he's actually met before, and it needs several uncontested seconds to work at all.
students.personality: Quiet and a little odd, most comfortable when he's looking for something rather than talking to someone. Doesn't do small talk; will happily talk for ten minutes about the best way to find a person in a crowd. Counts exits in any room he enters, out loud, under his breath, without meaning to. Sits near the window, apparently distracted, actually just half-scanning the room out of habit.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Iron Claws vs Search. Aikawa is fast, loud, and closes distance before most people register she's moving — exactly the kind of opponent Hama's slow, still-required searching has no good answer for. She doesn't clock him as a threat until he's already told his team exactly where she is.
students.sports_festival_role: Reconnaissance and target-location support in any team-based event — before he throws a single attack, he's usually already told his side where everyone else on the field is. In the tournament bracket, opponents who close distance fast and stay aggressive give him no window to actually use his Quirk.
students.tier1_appearance: A hallway monitor reviews footage of an empty corridor and insists someone must have walked through it, because the door at the far end opens on its own. Hama is seen a minute later, several floors away, looking unbothered.
students.dm_notes: Hama should feel genuinely useful in prep and genuinely vulnerable once a fight actually starts — his information is often better than his own follow-through. His rivalry with Aikawa is a clean 'speed denies setup' dynamic.
signature_moves: Locate (Action, concentration): senses direction and rough distance of a known person or object within 100ft, through obstacles.
Read the Room (Bonus Action): advantage on his next Perception/Investigation check in his current location.
Second Sight (Passive): his true eyes never need to be described as closed — cannot be surprised while his Locate is active.

students.name: Naza Keiseki

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Strength and size scale directly with ambient darkness and shrink sharply in bright light or direct sun — in full daylight the shadow is barely more than a passive haze, and if it ever acts against his direct will, he must succeed a Wisdom save to regain control before it acts again.

abilities.name: Shadow Strike
abilities.description: The shadow lashes out at a target within 15 feet: 2d8 + Charisma modifier necrotic damage. Damage and reach both scale up in darkness and are halved in bright light.

abilities.name: Loom
abilities.description: The shadow expands to loom over him, granting him half cover from attacks originating outside its reach; in bright light this cover is negligible.

students.quirk_summary: A dark, faintly-formed entity clings to Naza's shoulders and answers to him — mostly. In low light it grows large and genuinely dangerous, striking with a strength he can't match on his own. In bright light it shrinks to something barely useful. He's spent years learning to keep it on a short leash, because on the rare occasion it's acted on its own, the results weren't something he's eager to repeat.
students.personality: Controlled and deliberate, treats his own Quirk less like a companion and more like a tool he's spent years learning to keep leashed. Sits wherever the lighting is dimmest without seeming to choose it on purpose. Calm even when the shadow gets loud — he's the one talking it back down, not the other way around. Narrates instructions to it under his breath in a flat, patient tone, like a handler with a large dog.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Stress vs Dark Shadow. Both of them get more dangerous the longer a fight runs and the more pressure builds — Chozen through accumulated damage, Naza through his shadow slipping further off the leash. Whoever ends the fight fastest denies the other's whole strategy. Neither has thought about it in exactly those terms yet, but Matsunami has.
students.sports_festival_role: A heavy melee threat in low light, drastically weaker under bright arena lighting or direct sun — his effectiveness swings hard with the environment. In the tournament bracket, forcing a fight into full daylight is the single most reliable way to blunt him.
students.tier1_appearance: A faint dark haze clings to his shoulders even at rest in the dorm hallway, never quite lying flat, gone the moment someone flips on the overhead lights.
students.dm_notes: Naza is a heavy hitter whose power output should be visibly, mechanically tied to describable lighting conditions — telegraph his combat strength in real time by narrating the room's light. His rivalry with Chozen is conceptual: two escalation-based fighters, only one of whom controls his own trigger.
signature_moves: Shadow Strike (Action): 2d8 + CHA necrotic, range 15ft, scaling with ambient darkness.
Loom (Bonus Action): half cover from outside the shadow's reach, negligible in bright light.
Off the Leash (Passive): in near-total darkness, once per encounter the shadow can act on its own initiative unless Naza succeeds a WIS save to hold it.

students.name: Mawa Hisaya

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Prolonged use raises her own core temperature — after sustaining ignition for more than three consecutive rounds, she must succeed a DC 13 Constitution save or take 1d8 fire damage from her own heat and gain one level of exhaustion.

abilities.name: Ignite
abilities.description: Her skin catches and holds a controlled fire for up to one minute. Unarmed strikes deal an additional 1d6 fire damage, and she sheds bright light in a 15-foot radius.

abilities.name: Flare Guard
abilities.description: When hit by a melee attack, the attacker takes 1d6 fire damage from the heat radiating off her skin.

students.quirk_summary: Mawa's skin ignites at will, holding a controlled burn without harming her — her fists come out swinging hot, and anything that gets close enough to hit her gets burned in return. She can dial it down to something closer to 'warm' when she wants to, but her default setting under any real pressure is all the way up.
students.personality: Warm in every sense — generous, a little hot-tempered, quick to laugh and quicker to get in someone's face on a teammate's behalf. Loud in a likable way; the kind of person study groups form around without meaning to. Fights like she's protecting something even when she isn't — aggressive, forward, closes distance fast. Her hands warm up slightly whenever she's annoyed, well before she's aware of it herself.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Dragon vs Fire Skin. Both of them run hot, literally and otherwise — the obvious question everyone asks is whose fire actually wins in a straight contest. Neither of them has answered it yet, mostly because Matsunami keeps scheduling their sparring sessions for different weeks.
students.sports_festival_role: A front-line aggressor who trades damage confidently in extended close-range exchanges. In the tournament bracket, opponents who can stall or extend a fight long enough are working with the clock — her own heat becomes a liability well before most opponents' stamina runs out.
students.tier1_appearance: Seen warming her hands over a dorm kettle that was already boiling, just because the extra heat felt nice, entirely unbothered by the redundancy.
students.dm_notes: Mawa is a straightforward aggressive striker with a real self-imposed clock — track her rounds of sustained ignition and let the exhaustion cost land as a genuine consequence, not a formality.
signature_moves: Ignite (Bonus Action): unarmed strikes deal +1d6 fire damage for up to one minute; sheds light in a 15ft radius.
Flare Guard (Reaction, while Ignite active): melee attackers against her take 1d6 fire damage.
Simmer (Passive): can hold Ignite at reduced intensity indefinitely with no exhaustion risk, dealing no bonus damage but still shedding light and warmth.

students.name: Koto Kohomi

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Sustained spin builds up disorientation of her own — after two consecutive rounds at full spin, she has disadvantage on her next attack roll or Dexterity save unless she spends a round decelerating first.

abilities.name: Spin Up
abilities.description: Begins spinning at high velocity. While spinning, she has resistance to bludgeoning damage from any single source and imposes disadvantage on opportunity attacks made against her.

abilities.name: Centrifugal Sweep
abilities.description: A wide sweeping strike against all creatures within 10 feet: 1d10 + Dexterity modifier bludgeoning damage, Strength save or knocked back 10 feet.

students.quirk_summary: Koto can spin her whole body at speeds that shouldn't be structurally reasonable, using the momentum both to deflect incoming hits and to lash out in a wide, sweeping arc. She rarely moves in a straight line once she's spinning — the whole fight bends around her instead.
students.personality: Playful and a little chaotic, treats most problems like they can be solved by moving fast enough at them. Restless in her chair, always half-turned toward whoever's talking. Fights in circles, literally — rarely holds a straight line, which makes her hard to read and occasionally hard for her to control. Spins a pen between her fingers nonstop when she's thinking.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Tail vs Gyrate. Isokono's tail gives her grip and leverage in close — Koto's spin makes her a genuinely bad thing to grab onto. The fight comes down to whether Isokono can time a grapple for the split second Koto has to decelerate, or whether Koto can keep the spin going long enough that the window never opens.
students.sports_festival_role: Disruptive in any close-quarters or grappling-heavy event — hard to pin down, hard to hold. In the tournament bracket, ranged opponents who never let her close distance take away most of what makes her dangerous.
students.tier1_appearance: Seen spinning in slow, deliberate circles in the practice yard, timing herself, visibly frustrated at exactly the two-minute mark every single time.
students.dm_notes: Koto's disorientation clock is the fair counterplay — telegraph it (two rounds of spin, then a vulnerable beat) so smart players can time around it. Her rivalry with Isokono is a timing puzzle for both sides.
signature_moves: Spin Up (Bonus Action): resistance to bludgeoning damage from a single source while spinning; disadvantage on opportunity attacks against her.
Centrifugal Sweep (Action, while spinning): 10ft radius, 1d10 + DEX bludgeoning, STR save or knocked back 10ft.
Overspin (Passive): after two consecutive rounds spinning, disadvantage on her next attack or DEX save unless she decelerates first.

students.name: Moshita Maro

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Physical contact is required to copy a Quirk, and each copied power fades after two minutes. Accumulation- or mutation-based Quirks cannot be properly replicated, and upon copying he inherits all of its drawbacks, requiring a successful DC 16 Athletics check — on a failure, he cannot attempt to copy that specific Quirk again for seven rounds.

abilities.name: Mimic Touch
abilities.description: When he lands an unarmed strike on a creature, he may copy their Quirk. The copied Quirk lasts two minutes (three at 5th level, five at 10th level).

abilities.name: Quirk Swap
abilities.description: Switches between stored copied Quirks. He may maintain up to two copied Quirks at once, increasing by one additional Quirk at 5th and 10th level.

students.quirk_summary: Moshita can borrow a Quirk by landing a hit on its user — for two minutes he has full use of whatever ability they're carrying. He's spent years cataloguing how other people's powers actually work in practice, which means he rarely copies something he doesn't already know how to use well. He can't copy mutation- or accumulation-based Quirks, and copying anything risky means inheriting its drawbacks too.
students.personality: Earnest and quietly hungry to prove himself, very aware that his Quirk is 'someone else's' every time he uses it and determined not to let that be the whole story. Studies other students' Quirks the way some people study for exams — genuinely, thoroughly, without any of it being personal. Keeps a private notebook ranking every Quirk he's copied by how useful it was; 1-A's Quirks already take up several pages.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Steel vs Copy. The obvious play against Kazama is to land a hit and copy Steel — except copying him barely helps on its own. Moshita would still have to land that hit while Kazama's already hardened and absorbing exactly the kind of damage he's trying to dish out, then spend two minutes being just as hard to put down as his rival already is. Kazama knows this, which means the real fight is about whether Moshita can find an opening before he hardens, or simply outlast his daily uses.
students.sports_festival_role: Adaptive to a fault — his ceiling is whatever he's copied, which makes him either the biggest threat on the field or the least depending entirely on his last hit. In the tournament bracket, he's a puzzle encounter: opponents have to avoid giving him a clean touch while he's actively hunting for the most dangerous Quirk in reach.
students.tier1_appearance: A 1-A student swears a classmate tagged them with a light shove in a sparring drill, then suddenly fought unlike themselves for thirty seconds. Nobody can prove it was Moshita. If directly confronted: 'I don't know what you're referring to,' delivered in someone else's exact cadence.
students.dm_notes: Moshita is a slow-burn reveal — his Tier 1 appearances should all be deniable, easy to write off as imagination. By the Sports Festival, players should be actively wary of letting him land a hit.
signature_moves: Mimic Touch (Bonus Action): on landing an unarmed strike, copy the target's Quirk for two minutes. Cannot copy mutation/accumulation Quirks; inherits copied drawbacks.
Quirk Swap (Bonus Action): switches which copied Quirk is active; can hold up to two in reserve.
Cold Read (Passive): advantage on the Athletics check required when first copying a Quirk he's observed the target use before.

students.name: Isosato Sari

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Constructs take a full round to solidify from soft to load-bearing, and their structural strength is capped by how much pressure she can compress into them at once — enough concentrated force applied before a construct fully solidifies simply breaks through it.

abilities.name: Compress
abilities.description: Condenses a solid air construct — a wall, platform, or set of stairs, up to 10 feet in any dimension — within 30 feet. It has AC 14 and 20 HP, and fully solidifies at the start of her next turn.

abilities.name: Quick Step
abilities.description: Condenses a small platform directly beneath a creature's feet within 15 feet, instantly usable, granting them 10 feet of vertical or lateral movement they wouldn't otherwise have.

students.quirk_summary: Isosato compresses ordinary air into solid, load-bearing shapes — walls, platforms, stairs — fast enough to reshape a battlefield mid-fight. It looks unassuming until someone tries to walk through a wall that wasn't there a second ago. She thinks in load-bearing angles the way most people think in words.
students.personality: Methodical and quietly confident, thinks in shapes and structural angles before she thinks in anything else. The one who actually reads the structural engineering sidebar in the textbook for fun. Builds before she attacks — a wall, a step, a ledge — and expects the fight to happen on terrain she chose. Sketches little floor plans in the corner of every worksheet, entirely unconsciously.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Hologram vs Solid Air. Both of them build things that aren't quite what they first appear to be — Ichitaka's projections trick the eye, Isosato's constructs are real and load-bearing the moment someone touches them. The fight is a question of whether his illusions can bait her into wasting a construct on something that turns out to be fake.
students.sports_festival_role: Battlefield control and support — conjured platforms, walls, and stairs reshape terrain in her team's favor on the fly. In the tournament bracket, opponents who can apply enough concentrated force before a fresh construct solidifies get through her defenses before they're actually up.
students.tier1_appearance: A stepstool made of faintly shimmering, perfectly clear material is found propping open a supply closet door — solid to the touch, invisible from three feet away, gone by the next morning.
students.dm_notes: Isosato rewards creative use — let players describe unusual problems (a gap to cross, a chokepoint to seal) and have her improvise a construct for it. Her one-round solidify delay is the fair counterplay; telegraph it clearly.
signature_moves: Compress (Action): conjures a solid air construct up to 10ft in any dimension within 30ft; AC 14, 20 HP, fully solid at start of her next turn.
Quick Step (Bonus Action, 5th level): instant small platform under an ally's feet within 15ft, granting 10ft of otherwise-unavailable movement.
Load-Bearing Eye (Passive): advantage on checks to judge whether a structure or surface can hold weight.

students.name: Yamaru Todao

quirk_mechanics.weakness: The endurance delays damage rather than preventing it — once his hidden threshold is exceeded, he collapses suddenly and completely rather than gradually, with no warning sign visible to anyone who hasn't studied him closely.

abilities.name: Push Through
abilities.description: Once per encounter, when he would be reduced to 0 HP, he instead drops to 1 HP and remains conscious and functional.

abilities.name: Ignore It
abilities.description: When he takes damage, he can choose to treat any resulting condition (prone, stunned, frightened) as not applying to him until the end of his next turn, at the cost of taking 1d4 additional damage from the same hit.

students.quirk_summary: Yamaru's body simply keeps functioning past the point where most people's would stop — pain registers, damage registers, but none of it changes his output until he's genuinely out of runway. A pale, faintly grey undertone spreads across his skin the longer a fight runs, the only outward sign that anything's actually catching up to him.
students.personality: Grim-sounding Quirk name, easygoing guy — Yamaru's one of the more relaxed people in the class, mostly because very little rattles him anymore. Falls asleep in the back row more than any teacher's comfortable with and somehow still passes. Takes hits that should end a fight and just keeps standing there, unnerving for anyone who hasn't seen it before. Checks in with 'still here' as a running joke whenever someone asks if he's okay after getting hit.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Engine vs Deathly Endurance. Izuto's raw output vs Yamaru's near-total refusal to go down. The central question is whether Izuto can put enough force through him before his hidden threshold gets crossed, or whether Yamaru simply outlasts him past the point where Izuto's engines have anything left to give.
students.sports_festival_role: An attrition tank who keeps functioning at HP totals that would end most fights, brutal in long exchanges and unremarkable in short ones. In the tournament bracket, he and Izuto are the fight everyone in both classes has circled on the schedule.
students.tier1_appearance: Cafeteria during dorm move-in. Eats without hurry. Makes eye contact with no one. Once, in the corridor, he passes a 1-A student without acknowledging them. They don't notice. He does.
students.dm_notes: Yamaru is not a villain and not a bad person — he's the structural version of Masahata, someone whose quiet certainty about outlasting people is usually correct. Let his correctness be slightly unnerving rather than smug. His threshold-collapse should feel sudden and real when it finally happens, not telegraphed.
signature_moves: Push Through (Passive, once per encounter): drops to 1 HP instead of 0.
Ignore It (Reaction): shrugs off a resulting condition until the end of his next turn, taking 1d4 extra damage.
Grinding Pace (Passive): resistance to exhaustion effects and immune to being frightened.

students.name: Chisano Tomose

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Each wave takes a full action to build to a releasable force and telegraphs clearly in the moments before release — an opponent who closes distance during the buildup can reach her before the wave ever forms.

abilities.name: Build
abilities.description: Begins building a kinetic wave. At the start of her next turn, she may release it as a free action: a 20-foot cone dealing 2d8 + Wisdom modifier force damage, Strength save for half and no push, or full damage and pushed back 15 feet on a failure.

abilities.name: Ripple
abilities.description: When hit by a melee attack, releases a small kinetic pulse that pushes the attacker back 5 feet, no damage.

students.quirk_summary: Chisano builds and releases pulses of kinetic force in rolling waves — nothing instant, everything building, pressure that arrives a beat after it's earned. A visible ripple runs through the air around her palms right before release, the only warning she gives.
students.personality: Unhurried and even-tempered, moves and speaks like she's never once been in a rush and doesn't intend to start. The steadiest presence in group work, unfazed when plans change mid-project. Fights in rolling exchanges rather than sudden bursts, building pressure wave after wave instead of going for one big hit. Taps a rhythm against her leg with two fingers whenever she's building up to something.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Poltergeist vs Wave Motion. Nomi's precise telekinetic control doesn't need her own body to move at all — Chisano's raw kinetic waves are powerful but broad, and hard to aim as tightly as Nomi can move a single small object. The contest is control against power, and neither of them has convincingly won it yet.
students.sports_festival_role: A sustained-pressure ranged attacker who wears opponents down wave after wave rather than one-shotting them. In the tournament bracket, opponents who close distance fast during the buildup beat her before the wave ever forms.
students.tier1_appearance: The practice yard's target dummies are all leaning at the same subtle angle by the end of the week — nobody's caught her actually hitting any of them.
students.dm_notes: Chisano rewards patient, methodical DMing — let the buildup beat land as genuine tension, not a formality. Her rivalry with Nomi is a clean power-vs-precision framing worth revisiting if they ever cross paths on screen.
signature_moves: Build (Action, then released at start of next turn): 20ft cone, 2d8 + WIS force damage, STR save for half and no push.
Ripple (Reaction): pushes a melee attacker back 5ft, no damage.
Standing Wave (Passive): difficult terrain in a 10ft radius around her doesn't affect her own movement.

students.name: Hashige Tataka

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Only works on ferrous metal already present in the environment — in a fully non-metallic space, he has nothing to work with, and objects larger than roughly 200 pounds resist his control significantly, requiring a full action to move at all.

abilities.name: Reshape
abilities.description: Bends, redirects, or reforms up to 50 pounds of unattended metal within 60 feet into a barrier, weapon, or restraint. A reshaped weapon deals 1d8 + Intelligence modifier bludgeoning or slashing damage on his next attack; a barrier grants half or three-quarters cover.

abilities.name: Wire the Room
abilities.description: Extends fine control to every piece of metal in a 30-foot radius, sensing the exact position of any creature that moves through it and imposing disadvantage on Stealth checks made within the area.

students.quirk_summary: Hashige controls ferrous metal within his range, reshaping it into barriers, weapons, or restraints — and given enough of a room to work with, he can wire the whole space with fine, sensing control that tells him exactly where everyone in it is moving. Precise, methodical, and only as dangerous as the environment lets him be.
students.personality: Disciplined and a little rigid, treats his own Quirk like an extension of good posture — controlled, deliberate, never sloppy. Keeps his desk immaculate; can't stand a crooked stack of papers within reach, sometimes literally straightens them without thinking. Reshapes nearby metal into barriers or blades mid-fight, methodically rather than flashily. Absentmindedly bends paperclips into small sculptures during lectures.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Lightning vs Metal Manipulation. Hashige's reshaped metal conducts beautifully — if Nakaya lands a single arc on anything he's controlling, the current runs straight through his own working material. His counter is speed: sensing her closing and getting clear before contact turns their matchups into him staying one step ahead of someone who only needs to touch anything metal he's holding.
students.sports_festival_role: Devastating in any event with structure — he pre-rigs environments with reshaped metal during setup phases. In the tournament bracket, he's the student everyone is wary of facing in a room with anything metal in it at all.
students.tier1_appearance: Seen in the practice yard bending a stack of scrap rebar into a perfectly even lattice, checking each joint with a level before moving to the next.
students.dm_notes: Hashige is a versatile controller who scales hard with how much metal is actually in the environment — his Tier 1 weakness (U.A.'s wood-and-stone training grounds) should be a real, discoverable problem for him. His rivalry with Nakaya is a clean conduction-based hard counter.
signature_moves: Reshape (Action): reforms up to 50 lbs of unattended metal within 60ft into a weapon (1d8 + INT) or a barrier (half/three-quarters cover).
Wire the Room (Action, concentration): senses every creature moving through a 30ft radius of metal-wired terrain for up to one minute.
Ferrous Sense (Passive): can sense the rough location of significant metal objects within a wide radius without seeing them.

students.name: Asabira Magi

quirk_mechanics.weakness: A full storm takes several rounds of sustained concentration to build to its peak effect, and losing concentration at any point resets the buildup — she cannot generate anything beyond mild, harmless weather without a real ramp-up.

abilities.name: Gathering Storm
abilities.description: Begins generating localized weather in a 40-foot radius. Round 1: wind and overcast, no mechanical effect. Round 2: rain, difficult terrain and disadvantage on Perception (sight). Round 3+: lightning strikes a random creature in the area each round for 3d8 lightning damage (DC 15 Dexterity save for half).

abilities.name: Clear Skies
abilities.description: Instantly disperses any active weather effect, her own or otherwise, in a 60-foot radius.

students.quirk_summary: Asabira can generate genuine, localized weather — building from a change in wind through rain to a full lightning storm if she's given the time and the focus to get there. It's slow to reach its ceiling and entirely dependent on staying uninterrupted, but a fully formed storm changes the terms of an entire fight, not just her part of it.
students.personality: Dreamy and unhurried in conversation, but there's real weight under the softness — she's aware of exactly how much damage she could do and mostly chooses not to. Stares out windows more than any teacher is happy about, but it's less daydreaming than actually tracking the sky. Genuinely, physically can't lie about whether it's going to rain. Builds slowly — a change in wind, a drop in temperature, a first spit of rain — before the real weather arrives all at once.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Warp Gate vs Weather Manipulation. Zaro's protective fog is exactly the kind of ambient condition Asabira's Quirk was built to move through and clear — a strong enough wind could, in principle, strip the cover Zaro relies on to stay unseen. Neither of them has tested this directly. Asabira suspects it would work. She hasn't brought it up.
students.sports_festival_role: One of the most dangerous students at the Festival in any enclosed group event — a fully built storm reshapes visibility and terrain for the entire field, not just her immediate area. In the tournament bracket, her concentration requirement is the obvious target; break her focus early and she never gets past overcast skies.
students.tier1_appearance: The practice yard fills with unscheduled ground fog for exactly four minutes during her lunch break. No weather warning was issued. She apologises to a groundskeeper, who has stopped asking questions about it.
students.dm_notes: Asabira works best as a slow-building threat — give the weather time to visibly escalate before it matters, then let it dominate the back half of an encounter. Her concentration dependency is the fair counterplay; telegraph it clearly.
signature_moves: Gathering Storm (Action, concentration, escalates over rounds): wind → rain (difficult terrain, disadvantage on sight-based Perception) → lightning (3d8, DC 15 DEX save for half) by round 3.
Clear Skies (Action): disperses any weather effect in a 60ft radius, hers or otherwise.
Forecast (Passive): cannot be caught off guard by natural weather; always knows what's coming within the hour.

students.name: Achi Homei

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Echolocation only works on things loud enough to bounce sound back to him — genuinely silent environments or opponents give him nothing to work with, and a deafened Achi loses the ability entirely until the condition ends.

abilities.name: Echo Read
abilities.description: Emits a burst of sound at a pitch only he can properly interpret, mapping a 30-foot radius regardless of darkness, fog, or obstruction. He can perceive the shape and rough position of every creature and major object in the area for one round.

abilities.name: Shriek
abilities.description: A concentrated vocal blast in a 15-foot cone: 2d8 thunder damage, Constitution save or deafened until the end of the target's next turn.

students.quirk_summary: Achi's voice does more than talk — pitched and directed correctly, it maps a space through sound the way a bat reads a cave, letting him sense shapes and movement through darkness, fog, or obstruction that would blind anyone else. He talks constantly in a fight, not out of nerves; he's actively reading the room.
students.personality: Easygoing and a little scattered, genuinely doesn't mind being the odd one out — he's had a bat's head his whole life and stopped apologizing for it years ago. Naps in weird positions during free periods, upside-down more than once, and denies it every time someone brings it up. Tilts his head sharply toward any sudden sound before he can stop himself. Talks constantly mid-fight while actively mapping the space with his voice.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Iron Ball vs Voice. Setaka's attacks are heavy, telegraphed, and loud — exactly the kind of thing Achi hears coming from a mile off. The real contest is whether Setaka can land a hit quietly enough, or fast enough, that the sound arrives at the same moment as the blow instead of before it.
students.sports_festival_role: Battlefield awareness and disruption — echolocates through obstruction and darkness that would blind anyone else, and can loose a disorienting shriek at close range. In the tournament bracket, his echolocation depends on sound; a fight in a place that's already very loud, or an opponent who can dampen noise, takes away most of his advantage.
students.tier1_appearance: The dorm hallway lights flicker out during a blackout drill, and Achi is the only one who doesn't reach for a wall to orient himself, entirely unbothered by the dark.
students.dm_notes: Achi's echolocation is best run as a constant low-grade advantage — small warnings, correct guesses about layout, near-misses that look like luck. Keep the sound-dependency limitation visible so smart players can find the counter.
signature_moves: Echo Read (Bonus Action): maps a 30ft radius through darkness/fog/obstruction for one round.
Shriek (Action, recharge 5-6): 15ft cone, 2d8 thunder damage, CON save or deafened.
Never Lost (Passive): cannot become lost or disoriented while conscious, even blinded or in total darkness.

students.name: Zabata Haho

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Overextending too far or too fast leaves her limbs slow to retract for a full round, during which sudden forced movement against a fully stretched limb deals her an extra 1d6 damage.

abilities.name: Stretch
abilities.description: Extends a limb up to 15 feet, allowing melee attacks, grapples, or object interactions at that range this turn.

abilities.name: Slack
abilities.description: When hit by a bludgeoning or force effect, goes fully slack, taking half damage from that hit and automatically succeeding any save against being knocked prone or pushed by it.

students.quirk_summary: Zabata's body stretches, flattens, and compresses well past what it should be able to — an arm extended ten feet, a whole body gone momentarily slack to shrug off a hit, a gap too narrow for a person suddenly not a problem. She treats all of it as a fairly relaxed party trick, which undersells it badly.
students.personality: Loose and easygoing in a way that mirrors her Quirk almost too neatly — hard to pin down, hard to rattle, bends instead of breaking under pressure both physically and otherwise. Sprawls across her desk in postures that shouldn't be comfortable and somehow are. Cracks her knuckles by literally stretching each finger out an extra inch and letting it snap back. Deflects personal questions the same easy way she deflects punches.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Vines vs Elasticity. Kibi can bind and constrict from range — but something whose whole body can go slack and reshape itself is a genuinely bad thing to try to hold onto. The fight is a slow, relaxed contest between someone who wants to tie things down and someone who was never really solid to begin with.
students.sports_festival_role: A reach-based skirmisher whose extended limbs strike, grab, or trip from well outside normal range. In the tournament bracket, enough sudden force applied while she's fully stretched can genuinely injure her — the one real opening her style leaves.
students.tier1_appearance: Seen flattening her whole hand to slip a dropped key out from under a locked door, entirely bored by how impressive this should probably look to someone.
students.dm_notes: Zabata is a reach-and-mitigation specialist — let her extended-limb attacks feel genuinely unusual in range, and let Slack's damage reduction feel earned rather than automatic. Her rivalry with Kibi is a classic bind-vs-escape framing.
signature_moves: Stretch (Bonus Action): extends a limb up to 15ft for a melee attack, grapple, or object interaction this turn.
Slack (Reaction): halves damage from a bludgeoning/force hit and auto-succeeds saves against being knocked prone or pushed by it.
Narrow Fit (Passive): can compress her body to fit through any gap at least 6 inches wide.

students.name: Kagamo Akake

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Chaining propulsion bursts drains her fast — after three uses of Blast Off in a single encounter, each further use costs her 1d6 HP from the physical strain of the recoil.

abilities.name: Blast Off
abilities.description: Fires compressed air from her palms or heels, granting 20 feet of movement in any direction (including straight up) that doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

abilities.name: Palm Cannon
abilities.description: A concentrated blast at a target within 30 feet: 2d8 + Strength modifier bludgeoning damage, Strength save or pushed back 15 feet.

students.quirk_summary: Kagamo fires compressed air from her palms and heels — hard enough to propel herself in short, explosive bursts, or hard enough to hit like a battering ram at range. She uses both constantly, fighting like she's perpetually mid-jump.
students.personality: High-energy and competitive, treats nearly everything as something that can be timed, jumped, or raced. Can't sit still through a full lecture; taps out rhythms with her feet that drive the person next to her quietly insane. Always takes the stairs two at a time, Quirk or not. Loud, enthusiastic, no hidden agenda — the rare competitor who genuinely wants you to be good enough to make the fight worth having.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Comic vs Air Cannon. Both of them create loud, broad-area chaos that the crowd loves watching. They'll either be best friends or destroy each other immediately at the Festival — the exact circumstances of their first meeting will determine which. Either outcome is correct.
students.sports_festival_role: Devastating in group events that require movement or terrain control — her Palm Cannon and propulsion bursts create visible, dramatic shockwaves the audience loves. In the tournament bracket, chaining too many bursts costs her real HP from the recoil, a cost she's occasionally too excited to remember.
students.tier1_appearance: Two 7am blasts on move-in morning, felt through the dorm floor. If confronted: 'Warmup,' delivered as a complete explanation.
students.dm_notes: Kagamo is the relief — run her Tier 1 scenes as levity. She has no secrets, no agenda, no hidden depth to excavate. Give her a genuine crowd-pleasing moment at the Festival and let it be excellent.
signature_moves: Blast Off (Bonus Action): 20ft of propulsion movement in any direction, no opportunity attacks provoked.
Palm Cannon (Action): 30ft ranged blast, 2d8 + STR bludgeoning, STR save or pushed back 15ft.
Overdrive (Passive): after the third Blast Off in an encounter, each further use costs 1d6 HP from recoil strain.

students.name: Detsu Narumitsu

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Maintaining a creation requires ongoing concentration and physical stamina — if his concentration breaks or he's reduced below half HP, any active creations dissolve immediately, and he can only sustain creations totaling his level in Hit Dice at once.

abilities.name: Shape Beast
abilities.description: Manifests a beast construct (statistics equal to a CR 1/4 or lower beast of his choice) from ambient matter, which acts on his initiative and obeys his commands. Lasts until concentration breaks or the beast is reduced to 0 HP.

abilities.name: Dismiss & Reform
abilities.description: Dissolves an active creation and immediately shapes a new one of equal or lesser Hit Dice, without spending an action.

students.quirk_summary: Detsu can manifest short-lived beast constructs from nothing, shaped from something between mud and instinct, obeying him the moment they form. He directs more than he fights directly — sending creations in first, reading the field through them, trading personal risk for numbers.
students.personality: Quiet and gentle, more comfortable around what he creates than around people, though he's working on that. Doodles animals in every margin of every notebook, usually variations on things he's already made once. Names every single beast he creates, even the ones that only last a few minutes, and is genuinely a little sad when they go.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Dupli-Arms vs Beast Creation. Samitsu's extra limbs and Detsu's summoned creations both solve the same problem — needing more bodies on the field than one person actually has. Whoever manages that numbers advantage better, rather than whoever hits harder, tends to decide their matchups.
students.sports_festival_role: A summoner/controller who trades raw personal combat power for battlefield presence and numbers. In the tournament bracket, overwhelming his creations fast enough leaves him personally undefended with very little combat capability of his own.
students.tier1_appearance: A small, roughly-shaped clay bird is found perched on a 1-A student's windowsill, blinking once before it dissolves back into inert material. Nobody saw him do it.
students.dm_notes: Detsu rewards creative DMing — let players describe a problem and have him improvise a beast for it. His concentration and Hit Dice cap keep him grounded; track how much he's fielding in a given fight.
signature_moves: Shape Beast (Action, concentration): manifests a CR 1/4 or lower beast construct, obeying his commands.
Dismiss & Reform (Bonus Action): dissolves an active creation and shapes a new one of equal or lesser Hit Dice.
Kindly Maker (Passive): his creations never act with cruelty beyond what's needed to follow his commands, and can be shaped for non-combat utility.

students.name: Kukino Kaino

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Her bubbles and foam are easily disrupted by strong wind or open flame, which pops or burns through a field instantly — she has no way to reform a cleared field mid-fight faster than one section per action.

abilities.name: Foam Field
abilities.description: Fills a 15-foot radius within 30 feet with thick, slick foam. The area becomes difficult terrain, and creatures moving through it must succeed a Dexterity save or fall prone.

abilities.name: Bubble Burst
abilities.description: A cluster of bubbles pops around a target within 20 feet: no damage, but the target is blinded until the end of its next turn unless it succeeds a Constitution save.

students.quirk_summary: Kukino produces cleansing bubbles and foam that dissolve grime on contact and, applied differently, make an excellent mess of a battlefield — blinding bursts, treacherous slick footing, fields nobody wants to walk through. She thinks of it mostly as cleaning. It's also a genuinely dangerous crowd-control Quirk she hasn't fully clocked yet.
students.personality: Cheerful and tidy to a degree that borders on a personality trait all its own — genuinely cannot stand a dirty desk or an unresolved argument. The one who quietly wipes down shared equipment before anyone asks. Fights dirty in the cleanest possible way, delivering blinding foam with an apologetic smile. Blows an actual soap bubble absentmindedly whenever she's bored.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Twin Impact vs Clean Bubbler. Toragi's precision-timed strikes rely on solid, predictable footing to land — Kukino's foam takes exactly that away. The harder Toragi commits to a follow-through, the worse the footing gets underneath her.
students.sports_festival_role: Battlefield control through terrain denial — foam and bubble fields obscure vision and ruin footing more than they deal direct damage. In the tournament bracket, her fields are easily cleared by strong wind or fire, and she has no real answer once the field's been reset.
students.tier1_appearance: The dorm's common bathroom is spotless for the first time in living memory. Nobody asked her to do this. She seems confused that anyone would need to.
students.dm_notes: Kukino undersells her own combat usefulness by thinking of her Quirk as 'just cleaning' — she hasn't fully clocked how dangerous a battlefield she can make. Let her rivalry with Toragi hinge explicitly on footing.
signature_moves: Foam Field (Action): 15ft radius difficult terrain within 30ft; DEX save or fall prone when moving through it.
Bubble Burst (Bonus Action): target within 20ft is blinded until end of its next turn unless it succeeds a CON save.
Spotless (Passive): can dissolve most non-organic residue and minor stains on contact, at will, outside combat.

students.name: Hatashi Hamba

quirk_mechanics.weakness: The boost is small and universal rather than large and specialized — against any opponent who has trained a single stat far past its normal ceiling, his flat, modest advantage rarely wins a direct contest of that specific stat.

abilities.name: Balanced Output
abilities.description: All six ability scores and TECH are permanently increased by 1, and he has advantage on any check made specifically to compare his physical performance against a known baseline.

abilities.name: Steady Recovery
abilities.description: Regains an additional 1d4 HP whenever he spends a Hit Die, and recovers from exhaustion levels at twice the normal rate.

students.quirk_summary: Hatashi's every physical and mental faculty runs slightly, permanently better than baseline — reflexes, strength, memory, recovery, all of it nudged upward by the same small margin. No single spectacular trick, just reliably, measurably better than expected at nearly everything.
students.personality: Steady and unflashy, genuinely comfortable being the reliable one instead of the impressive one. Consistent — consistently on time, consistently prepared, consistently the person a study group can count on. Keeps a small notebook of exact numbers — personal bests, reaction times, grip strength — updated after every training session.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Neutralization vs High Specs. Kinosho can shut a Quirk down on contact — but there's very little to actually neutralize in Hatashi's case, since his advantage is baked into his own body rather than an active effect she can switch off. The fight becomes about whether her tactics still work against someone whose 'Quirk' barely reads as one.
students.sports_festival_role: A generalist who wins by being reliably slightly better across the board rather than spectacularly better at any one thing. In the tournament bracket, any single specialist playing to their one strength usually beats his flat advantage in a direct contest — he has to out-strategize, not out-stat.
students.tier1_appearance: Finishes every drone-wave exam drill a few seconds faster than projected, without ever looking like he's trying particularly hard.
students.dm_notes: Hatashi is the class's quiet backbone — people underestimate him right up until he's the one still standing. His rivalry with Kinosho hinges on her tactics not having an obvious lever to pull against him.
signature_moves: Balanced Output (Passive): +1 to every ability score and TECH; advantage on comparative physical-performance checks.
Steady Recovery (Passive): +1d4 HP when spending a Hit Die; exhaustion recovers twice as fast.
No Weak Link (Passive): never has disadvantage from a single poor ability score on a skill check requiring two.

students.name: Tateta Fumira

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Firing drains her fast — after three shots in a single encounter, each further shot costs her 1d4 HP, and she requires a clear line of sight to charge a shot properly; smoke, fog, or heavy obscurement prevents her from firing at all.

abilities.name: Charged Shot
abilities.description: A precise laser bolt at a target within 90 feet: 2d10 + Dexterity modifier radiant damage. Requires a clear line of sight to charge.

abilities.name: Signal Flare
abilities.description: Fires a low-intensity beam to mark a location or signal at range without dealing damage, visible up to a mile in clear conditions.

students.quirk_summary: Tateta fires precise, high-velocity laser bolts, each one aimed rather than sprayed. She reads a fight like a series of single shots that each need to count, which means she's usually thinking two exchanges ahead of whoever she's actually shooting at.
students.personality: Blunt and efficient, doesn't waste words any more than she wastes shots. Finishes tests early and spends the extra time re-checking her answers instead of the other way around. Squints and goes dead silent right before she takes a real shot, which her classmates have learned to treat as a countdown.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Water Gun vs Bullet Laser. Two ranged fighters who both live and die by keeping their distance and their aim clean — the fight comes down to whose accuracy actually holds up when the other person is shooting back just as precisely. Neither of them enjoys losing a marksmanship contest, and both are certain they won't.
students.sports_festival_role: Long-range precision damage that hits hard and accurate at range, at the cost of being fairly fragile up close. In the tournament bracket, smoke, fog, or an opponent closing the gap immediately takes away most of what makes her dangerous.
students.tier1_appearance: A target sixty feet down the practice range has a single, dead-center hole in it. Tateta is already walking away by the time anyone checks.
students.dm_notes: Tateta is a glass-cannon marksman — track her ammunition cost and her line-of-sight requirement carefully; running dry or losing sight mid-fight should be a real, discoverable consequence.
signature_moves: Charged Shot (Action): 90ft ranged attack, 2d10 + DEX radiant damage, requires clear line of sight.
Signal Flare (Bonus Action): non-damaging beam visible up to a mile, marks a location.
Steady Aim (Passive): after not moving on her turn, her next Charged Shot this encounter has advantage.

students.name: Detsami Doki

quirk_mechanics.weakness: Dries out and slows in prolonged heat or arid conditions — after ten minutes without access to water or moisture in a hot environment, his speed is halved and he has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity checks until he can rehydrate.

abilities.name: Long Tongue
abilities.description: Extends his tongue up to 20 feet to grab an object or creature (Small or smaller creatures must succeed a Strength save or be pulled 10 feet toward him), or to interact with something at range.

abilities.name: Wall Cling
abilities.description: Can climb difficult and vertical surfaces, including upside down along ceilings, without needing to make a check, at his normal speed.

students.quirk_summary: Detsami's body is built for amphibious mobility more than raw force — sticky skin for climbing anything, a long tongue for reach and grabbing, powerful legs for jumping, and genuinely excellent swimming. He treats most terrain as usable ground, because for him, most of it actually is.
students.personality: Blunt and matter-of-fact to the point that people sometimes mistake it for coldness — he just says the true thing first and worries about tone never. Answers questions other students are too embarrassed to ask, plainly, without self-consciousness. Sticks his tongue out slightly when thinking hard, entirely without noticing. Uses walls, water, and ceilings more than most, because for him, most of it counts as usable ground.
students.rivalry_dynamic: Double vs Frog. Yoshibara doubles herself to be in two places at once — Detsami doesn't need to, since walls, water, and ceilings all count as places he can already be that most people can't reach. The contest is numbers against access: whether two of her covers more ground than one of him going anywhere he wants.
students.sports_festival_role: A mobility and utility fighter who climbs, clings, and swims his way past terrain that stops everyone else. In the tournament bracket, an opponent who can force a long fight somewhere hot and dry has a real, discoverable advantage over him.
students.tier1_appearance: Found calmly eating lunch upside down on the dorm common-room ceiling. When asked why: 'The couch was taken.'
students.dm_notes: Detsami is best run as a mobility specialist who treats the whole environment as available terrain — let players see him use walls and ceilings casually, not just as a combat trick. His rivalry with Yoshibara is a fun numbers-vs-access framing.
signature_moves: Long Tongue (Action or Bonus Action): 20ft reach to grab an object or pull a Small-or-smaller creature 10ft (STR save negates the pull).
Wall Cling (Passive): climbs any surface, including ceilings, at full speed with no check required.
Amphibious (Passive): can breathe underwater indefinitely and swims at his full speed.
